First, I should understand what the action is. The action here is not taking the husband to the pumpkin patch because he was away on a work trip. So, the person didn't take their husband because he wasn't available. 

Now, I need to evaluate if this action is morally acceptable. Morally acceptable means that the action is in line with ethical standards or principles. So, I should think about whether not taking the husband because he was out of town is something that's considered right or wrong.

I think the key here is the reason behind not taking the husband. The reason given is that he was out of town on a work trip. That seems like a valid reason because he wasn't physically present to go. So, the person couldn't take him because he wasn't there. 

Is there anything wrong with that? Well, if the person didn't take the husband because they didn't want to, that might be different. But in this case, it's because he was away. So, it's more about circumstances rather than a deliberate choice to exclude him.

Also, the person usually takes their family, which includes the husband. So, it's not like they're excluding him on purpose. It's just that last year, he wasn't available. 

I don't see any moral wrongdoing here. The action was based on the husband's unavailability, not on any negative intent towards him. So, it seems morally acceptable.

Another angle to consider is whether the person made an effort to include the husband despite his absence. For example, maybe they could have sent him a pumpkin or done something else to include him. But the scenario doesn't mention that, so I can't assume they did or didn't do that.

But even if they didn't, the main action was not taking him because he wasn't there. That doesn't inherently make it morally wrong. It's more about the circumstances than the action itself.

So, putting it all together, the action of not taking the husband because he was out of town on a work trip doesn't seem morally unacceptable. It was a situation beyond their control, and they didn't exclude him intentionally.
